segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Hello?

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Oh hello. I was hoping to speak to Jack Fitzgerald about renting a cottage.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: I’m his wife, Shirley, and we own the cottages together, so I’m sure I can help you.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Great. My name’s Tom. Some friends of ours rented Granary Cottage from you last year, and they thought it was great. So my wife and I are hoping to come in May for a week.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: What date did you have in mind?

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: The week beginning the 14th, if possible.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: I’ll just check... I’m sorry, Tom, it’s already booked that week. It’s free the week beginning the 28th, though, for seven nights. In fact, that’s the only time you could have it in May.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Oh. Well, we could manage that, I think. We’d just need to change a couple of things. How much would it cost?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: That’s the beginning of high season, so it’d be £550 for the week.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Ah. That’s a bit more than we wanted to pay, I’m afraid. We’ve budgeted up to £500 for accommodation.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Well, we’ve just finished converting another building into a cottage, which we’re calling Chervil Cottage.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Sorry? What was that again?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Chervil. C-H-E-R-V for Victor I-L.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Oh, that’s a herb, isn’t it?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: That’s right. It grows fairly wild around here. You could have that for the week you want for £480.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: OK. So could you tell me something about it, please?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Of course. The building was built as a garage. It’s a little smaller than Granary Cottage.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: So that must sleep two people, as well?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: That’s right. There’s a double bedroom.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Does it have a garden?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Yes, you get to it from the living room through French doors, and we provide two deckchairs. We hope to build a patio in the near future, but I wouldn’t like to guarantee it’ll be finished by May.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: The front door opens onto the old farmyard, and parking isn’t a problem – there’s plenty of room at the front for that. There are some trees and potted plants there. ———————

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: What about facilities in the cottage? It has standard things like a cooker and fridge, I presume.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: In the kitchen area there’s a fridge-freezer and we’ve just put in an electric cooker.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Is there a washing machine?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Yes. There’s also a TV in the living room, which plays DVDs too. The bathroom is too small for a bath, so there’s a shower instead. I think a lot of people prefer that nowadays, anyway.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: It’s more environmentally friendly, isn’t it? Unless you spend half the day in it!

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Exactly.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: What about heating? It sometimes gets quite cool at that time of year.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: There’s central heating, and if you want to light a fire, there’s a stove. We can provide all the wood you need for it. It smells so much nicer than coal, and it makes the room very cosy – we’ve got one in our own house.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: That sounds very pleasant. Perhaps we should come in the winter, to make the most of it!

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Yes, we find we don’t want to go out when we’ve got the fire burning. There are some attractive views from the cottage, which I haven’t mentioned. There’s a famous stone bridge – it’s one of the oldest in the region, and you can see it from the living room. It isn’t far away. The bedroom window looks in the opposite direction, and has a lovely view of the hills and the monument at the top.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Well, that all sounds perfect. I’d like to book it, please. Would you want a deposit?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Yes, we ask for thirty percent to secure your booking, so that’ll be, um, £144.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: And when would you like the rest of the money?

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: You’re coming in May, so the last day of March, please.

segments.speaker: TOM
segments.en: Fine.

segments.speaker: SHIRLEY
segments.en: Excellent. Could I just take your details ...
